newsitem.title: SPAIN: INSTANT VIEW - Spain May CPI up 1.5 pct yr/yr.
newsitem.headline: INSTANT VIEW - Spain May CPI up 1.5 pct yr/yr.

text.p: Following are comments from economists after Spain's National Statistics Institute INE said on Friday the May Consumer Price Index (CPI) rose 0.1 from April for a 1.5 percent year-on-year rise.
These figures matched exactly economists' consensus forecasts in a Reuters survey.
In April, CPI rose 1.7 percent year-on-year.
MARCO PIANELLI, ECONOMIST AT NOMURA LONDON

"The best part of the downtrend in the inflation is now over...because the comparison with the second part of 1996 is not going to be so favourable as it has been for the first six months. Medium term you have other important elements such as wages...This situation does not justify such an aggressive easing of monetary policy as we've had so far.

"The Bank of Spain could also cut next week, but then with an official rate at 5.0 percent it would start to be more cautious. We'll start to get close to the end of the cycle, and further cuts will be slower...They'll look to the approval of the budget and to the wages trend and not just inflation."
CARMEN HERNANSANZ, ECONOMIST AT MERRILL LYNCH ESPANA

"The CPI was in line with our forecasts and the core rate slightly worse. I think the Bank of Spain will wait until the Amsterdam (European Union) summit is over and see how the stability pact issue is resolved. There are still a few questions and I don't think it will cut rates at Monday's (repo) auction, but it could make a 25 basis point move at the next one, as uncertainties clear"
HEATHER RICHARDSON, ECONOMIST AT UBS IN LONDON

"The numbers were exactly as expected...One of the finance ministry officials also said 1.5 percent a few days ago so it wasn't a surprise. There was no evidence of swine fever which we were a little afraid of.

"We're saying no to a rate cut next week given (European economic and monetary union) uncertainty and some statements recently that the Bank of Spain wants to make sure inflation is moderate medium term. There will be a slight pick-up in summer. I think this could be the low.
"We do think there is scope for future rate cuts but not next week."
WILLIAM THORNILL, ECONOMIST AT TECHNICAL DATA LONDON
"The CPI is in line with market expectations and also as predicted by Montoro, so there are no surprises. This level is perhaps going to be the lowest level of the year.

"In terms of potential for another rate cut..if one month ago we had a 90 percent chance now there is a 50 percent chance. Basically we have all the problems surrounding Europe, there's a bit of uncertainty there, and also it's less important to ease rates now. I would say a weak no (to a rate cut next week)"
YOLANDA FERNANDEZ, ECONOMIST AT ANALISTAS FINANCIEROS

"...this hasn't changed our expections for the rest of the year, with the possibility of a slight pick-up in the year-on-year rate to 1.9 percent at year-end, with the core rate staying around the present level.

If the core rate had been slightly better than expected, we'd go for a cut in the key rate on Monday. But as this wasn't the case, the other factor will weigh, that's the euro and the markets, and prudence by the Bank of Spain will be useful so it can keep a margin until the next (repo) auction."
